answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The atlas multiplier is published, charged in river, and juniper lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 2524 identities would post 3451 proofs and burn roughly 86 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
